metadata.section: 11.7 Rights of way - the practical gateway

chunks.content:
11.8 Nca 2003 sections 135-137
Section 135 - approvals
A licensee may require approvals of a State Government, Local Government or other relevant
authority for installing, placing, laying or maintaining network facilities on, through, under or across
land. The responsibility for obtaining those approvals rests on the licensee. The section therefore
defeats the assumption that an NCC licence substitutes for every land or works approval.
Section 136 - duty of care
Take reasonable steps to cause as little detriment, inconvenience and damage as practicable.
Restore affected land to a condition similar to that before the activity.
Use good engineering practice and protect persons and property.
Minimise interference with utilities, roads, paths, traffic and use of land.
Protect the environment.
Make reasonable efforts to agree with public utilities on activities likely to affect their operations.
Section 137 - access to facilities and rights of way
A licensee must provide another licensee non-discriminatory access to a post, network facility or right
of way it owns or controls. Access may be denied on a non-discriminatory basis for insufficient
capacity or reasons of safety, security, reliability, or technical/engineering difficulty. NCC may make a
binding ruling in a licensee dispute and may regulate just and reasonable rates, terms and conditions.
The jurisdictional qualification
Section 137(5) states that the section does not confer NCC jurisdiction over access to posts, facilities
or rights of way where a State, local or other authority regulates the matter. A sound answer
acknowledges this federal-sector and land/corridor interface rather than claiming unlimited NCC
control.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   118
Issue   Correct reasoning
Access request refused   Test capacity and stated technical/safety basis; compare treatment of similar
seekers; seek evidence and alternatives.
Rate dispute   Identify asset/control, applicable authority, cost and comparators; pursue the
competent dispute route.
Road damaged   Section 136 restoration and good-engineering duties remain relevant
regardless of broadband objective.
Permit delay   Section 135 puts approval responsibility on licensee; wider coordination may
be needed, not fictional NCC permit power.
The section 137 access duty is strong but not absolute, and NCC's role is expressly
qualified by subsection (5).

11.9 Open access, sharing and infrastructure companies
Open access seeks to make infrastructure available to eligible users on transparent, fair and
non-discriminatory terms. It can reduce duplicate civil works, accelerate entry and increase utilisation.
It does not mean zero price, unlimited capacity or forced access without regard to safety and
technical feasibility.
Model   Meaning
Passive sharing   Duct, pole, tower, chamber, dark fibre or site is shared without a complete
active service.
Active sharing   Certain electronic/network functions or capacity are shared, subject to licence,
competition, security and operational controls.
Dark-fibre lease   Customer supplies/controls lighting equipment under the agreement.
Managed capacity   Provider lights and operates the network and sells bandwidth/service levels.
Indefeasible right of use   Long-term contractual right to use specified capacity/fibre; legal detail and risk
allocation matter.
Co-build   Parties jointly fund construction and allocate ducts, strands, costs and
maintenance.
Infrastructure Company concept
Nigeria's Infrastructure Company approach was designed around wholesale, open-access
metropolitan or regional fibre infrastructure. For examination, understand the regulatory logic: shared
backbone, wholesale neutrality, transparent access, coverage obligations, service levels and
investment support. Do not memorise an old number of regional licences as a timeless current fact;
licence status, restructuring and policy direction require current official verification.
Non-discrimination
Equivalent seekers should receive equivalent information, process, quality and price unless
objectively different circumstances justify different treatment. A vertically integrated owner must not
favour its retail affiliate through delay, inferior service, hidden rebates or advance information.

Access reference offer
A useful offer describes products, locations, technical interfaces, ordering, provisioning, service
levels, repair, capacity reservation, price, confidentiality, security, forecasting, termination and dispute
escalation. Publication alone is insufficient if actual practice differs.
Sharing is a competition tool and an engineering arrangement. Poorly designed sharing can create
a monopoly bottleneck or correlated failure; good sharing preserves investment incentives and
accountable service.

11.10 Economics, finance and commercial viability
Concept   Application
Capital expenditure   Up-front survey, design, permits, duct/cable, chambers, equipment, buildings
and construction.
Operating expenditure   Power, leases, maintenance, security, staff, repairs, software and route fees.
Take-up   Share of serviceable premises or organisations that actually subscribe.
Average revenue per user   Revenue must be interpreted with collection, churn and service cost.
Anchor tenant   Large predictable buyer improves bankability but may create concentration
risk.
Cost of capital   Risk and financing return required; regulatory uncertainty can increase it.
Sunk cost   Irrecoverable past cost should not alone justify future inefficient decisions.
Wholesale price reasoning
A sustainable access price should consider efficient cost, operating risk, capacity, useful life,
demand, quality and reasonable return while avoiding monopoly extraction or predatory exclusion.
Cost-plus, benchmarking and price-cap approaches answer different questions; no one formula fits
every facility.
Rural viability
Low density, long routes, difficult terrain, lower income, power/security cost and uncertain demand
can make purely commercial deployment unattractive. Responses include targeted universal-service
support, shared backbone, demand aggregation, competitive subsidy, public assets and
technology-neutral solutions. Support should be gap-based, measurable, time-controlled and
competitively neutral.
Business case sensitivity
Test lower take-up, construction delay, foreign-exchange exposure and cost escalation.
Model route cuts, repair and service-credit cost.
Separate committed contracts from non-binding demand forecasts.
Include permit renewal, restoration and decommissioning liabilities.
Avoid counting the same public support or customer twice.
Lower right-of-way cost improves economics but does not by itself prove investment,
affordability, coverage or adoption. Trace the causal chain and verify the outcome.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   120

11.11 Build, accept and maintain the network
Stage   Essential controls
Need and route study   Demand, endpoints, alternatives, geography, hazards, utilities and future road
plans.
Design   Topology, capacity, duct/strand plan, optical budget, crossings, resilience,
power and security.
Approvals and agreements   Correct authorities, land interests, utility coordination, environmental/traffic
conditions and access rights.
Procurement   Specifications, type/quality evidence, contractor competence, warranties and
change control.
Construction   Method statement, permits-to-work, depth/separation, chambers, markers,
safety, supervision and daily records.
Testing/acceptance   Loss/reflectometry results, service and protection tests, defect closure and
signed acceptance criteria.
Handover   Accurate as-builts, asset register, spares, training, contacts, warranties and
maintenance plan.
Operations   Monitoring, preventive work, fault localisation, dispatch, restoration, root
cause and recurring-risk treatment.
Change control
Field conditions frequently force route or material changes. Every deviation should be technically
assessed, approved at the correct level and reflected in as-built records. An undocumented shortcut
becomes an outage and accountability risk.
Reinstatement
Temporary repair should protect public safety immediately; permanent reinstatement should match
the road or land specification. Inspection, defect-liability periods and restoration bonds can protect the
authority, but they should not become opaque duplicate charges.
Asset records
A reliable geographic information system links coordinates, depth, route, ducts, strands, joints,
ownership, permits, capacity, condition and maintenance history. Access must be controlled because
detailed route data can be security-sensitive.
Contractor governance
The licensee remains accountable for statutory and licence obligations performed through
contractors. Prequalification, supervision, safety reporting, evidence retention and sanctions for
unsafe or unrecorded work are essential.
A project is not complete when cable is buried. It is complete when accepted performance, lawful
access, accurate records and maintainable operations are demonstrable.

chunks.content:
11.12 Cuts, vandalism, CNII and service continuity
Fibre cuts can result from road construction, other utilities, vandalism, theft attempts, poor route data,
erosion or operator error. The symptom may affect mobile voice/data, banking, government services
and emergency communications far from the cut.
Control layer   Examples
Prevent   Route coordination, markers, adequate depth/protection, permit control,
contractor awareness, patrols and community engagement.
Detect   Optical alarms, traffic monitoring, route sensors where justified, incident
reports and correlated customer alarms.
Respond   Locate, make safe, reroute, dispatch splicing team, communicate, preserve
evidence and restore priority service.
Recover   Permanent repair, test, capacity normalisation, customer remedy and
accurate record update.
Learn   Root-cause analysis, repeat-location trend, authority/contractor engagement
and design change.
Critical National Information Infrastructure
The 2024 designation of specified communications and digital infrastructure as Critical National
Information Infrastructure strengthens the national-protection context. It does not replace routine
engineering, land approval, maintenance, safety, incident reporting or evidence. Criminal-protection
measures and regulatory service obligations operate together.
Route diversity and priority
Operators should identify high-impact routes and dependent services, test alternate capacity and plan
spares. Restoration priority must be objective and documented; switching all traffic onto a backup can
overload it, so degraded-mode capacity matters.
Incident communication
Report verified impact, affected geography/services, start time, mitigation, expected updates and final
root cause without exposing exploitable route detail. Early estimates should be labelled. Closing an
incident requires stable restoration and follow-up, not merely disappearance of an alarm.
Public works coordination
Shared mapping and advance notice between roads agencies, utilities and operators can prevent
excavation damage. The NCC portal and intergovernmental coordination can improve transparency,
while each authority and operator remains responsible within its legal competence.
Calling every outage 'vandalism' without evidence obstructs prevention. Distinguish
malicious damage, accidental excavation, engineering defect, environmental event and
operational error.

chunks.content:
11.13 Policy chronology and 2026 status control
Instrument/initiative   How to treat it
National Telecommunications Policy
2000
Historical policy foundation for liberalisation, private investment and expanded
access.
Nigerian Communications Act 2003   Operative primary legal foundation; use sections 135-137 and other relevant
powers directly.
National Broadband Plan 2013-2018   Historical first-plan period; achievements or shortfalls require evidence, not
present-tense treatment.
Nigerian National Broadband Plan
2020-2025
Completed plan period as at September 2026. Its targets remain examinable
historically but are not automatically today's operative targets.
National Broadband Alliance for
Nigeria
Current-era coordination initiative intended to align public and private action
around broadband adoption and infrastructure; verify live commitments and
measured results.
Project Bridge / national fibre
proposals
Treat announced structure, financing and route scale as
programme/transaction status until official evidence shows contracted, built, lit
and accepted kilometres.
NCC Ease of Doing Business portal   Current transparency mechanism for state-level right-of-way and
infrastructure-deployment information; verify portal data date before quoting
figures.
Five status labels
Historical - once applicable or completed period.
Operative - presently legally in force.
Approved/current programme - authorised and underway, but not necessarily delivered.
Draft/consultation - proposed and not final law merely because published.
Achievement - independently or officially evidenced completed outcome.
Targets versus results
A plan's coverage, speed or penetration target expresses intended future outcome. Progress
reporting must state the measurement method and date. An announced route length may refer to
proposed, financed, trenched, cable-laid, accepted, lit or service-carrying infrastructure—each is a
different milestone.
Current-source discipline
For the final examination build, reconcile NCC, Federal Ministry, USPF, official gazettes/instruments
and programme transaction records. Use current figures only with date, definition and source. Do not
convert a ministerial aspiration, procurement notice or stakeholder statement into achieved national
coverage.
Version control is substantive knowledge. A candidate who knows a target but misstates its legal
or implementation status can give a confident yet wrong policy answer.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   123

11.14 Regulatory diagnosis and intervention
Observed problem   Evidence before intervention
High right-of-way cost   Published schedule, invoices, legal basis, comparable states, project
economics and duplicated charges.
Permit delay   Complete application date, service standard, queries, authority workflow,
dependencies and escalation.
Refused duct/fibre access   Ownership/control, capacity records, technical reason, comparable
applicants, price/terms and competent authority.
Slow broadband   End-user tests, busy-hour utilisation, radio/access condition, backhaul, core,
peering, device and application.
Repeated fibre cuts   Mapped incidents, cause, works permits, route/depth, offender, repair time
and prevention actions.
Unserved area   Serviceability data, demand, terrain, power, existing assets, viable
technologies and efficient funding gap.
Intervention ladder
Clarify obligations and data definitions.
Coordinate competent authorities and remove procedural friction.
Require transparency and non-discriminatory reference terms.
Resolve a statutory access dispute within jurisdiction.
Use licence, competition, quality or compliance powers where legal tests are met.
Apply targeted support where the market cannot efficiently close an evidenced gap.
Monitor outcome and redesign if consumer benefit does not materialise.
Competition assessment
Infrastructure can be an enduring bottleneck because duplication is costly. Assess market
boundaries, control, capacity, alternatives, switching, entry barriers and vertical incentives before
imposing access remedies. Mandatory access set too cheaply may discourage investment; access
set too high or discriminatorily may protect market power.
Technology neutrality
Specify the public outcome—capacity, availability, coverage, affordability or resilience—while
permitting suitable technologies, unless a technical or security reason justifies prescription. Fibre may
be preferred for backbone longevity without assuming it is the efficient final link everywhere.
NCC should not use a desirable policy outcome to bypass statutory jurisdiction or
procedure. Identify the competent actor and lawful instrument.

11.15 Applied level 10 scenarios
Scenario 1 - Full signal bars, unusable data
Do not order more towers reflexively. Establish time/location/device pattern; test radio quality and cell
utilisation; inspect site backhaul, core and external service paths; separate coverage from capacity;
assign remediation to the responsible layer and verify busy-hour improvement.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   124
Scenario 2 - State charges a new route fee
Confirm the legal instrument, asset/corridor, rate basis, affected approvals and section 135 boundary.
Quantify deployment effect, compare transparent practice and coordinate at the appropriate
intergovernmental level. Do not state that the NCC licence automatically nullifies state approval.
Scenario 3 - Duct owner refuses competitor
Confirm both are licensees, ownership/control and competent authority. Require capacity and
safety/technical evidence; examine equivalent treatment and feasible augmentation. Apply section
137 dispute/rate powers only within its subsection (5) qualification and give written reasons.
Scenario 4 - Government reports 5,000 km 'delivered'
Ask whether this means designed, trenched, cable installed, tested, accepted, lit or carrying service;
identify endpoints, route duplication and date. Report each milestone separately and connect it to
serviceable premises and use.
Scenario 5 - Rural fibre has no customers
Examine route relevance, wholesale offer, last-mile availability, retail affordability, devices, power,
skills and anchor demand. The solution may be open access, distribution build, demand aggregation
or targeted support—not another parallel backbone.
Scenario 6 - Two diverse circuits fail together
Map physical routes and common facilities; identify shared trench, bridge, equipment, power or
vendor control; redesign failure-domain diversity and test failover under load.
Scenario 7 - Road contractor repeatedly severs fibre
Preserve incident evidence; verify markings, depth, as-builts and works notice; coordinate
roads/utility processes; pursue applicable protection/enforcement routes; improve maps and safe-dig
control rather than relying only on penalties.
Scenario 8 - Operator advertises 'fibre coverage'
Define whether fibre passes an area, reaches a building or offers an orderable retail service. Test
installation time, price, capacity and exclusions. Prevent a network input from being represented as a
consumer outcome.
MODEL ANSWER FORMULA
Define outcome   →   map end-to-end layer   →   establish current legal/policy status   →   identify competent
actors   →   gather technical and economic evidence   →   select proportionate lawful intervention   →
measure user benefit and resilience.
Prompt   One-sentence core
Broadband   Reliable high-capacity connectivity

end-to-end layer   →   establish current legal/policy status   →   identify competent
actors   →   gather technical and economic evidence   →   select proportionate lawful intervention   →
measure user benefit and resilience.
Prompt   One-sentence core
Broadband   Reliable high-capacity connectivity outcome produced by an end-to-end
ecosystem, not one technology.
Backbone/backhaul/last mile   Long-haul core routes / aggregation from access toward core / final reach to
user.
Dark fibre   Installed unlit fibre, not a functioning service by itself.
Open access   Fair, transparent, non-discriminatory access on reasonable technical and
commercial terms—not free access.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   125
Prompt   One-sentence core
Right of way   Legal/authorised corridor access, distinct from land or infrastructure
ownership.
Section 135   Licensee is responsible for relevant state, local and other installation
approvals.
Section 136   Minimise harm; restore; use good engineering; protect safety, utilities, roads
and environment.
Section 137   Licensee-to-licensee non-discriminatory facility/ROW access, qualified
exceptions, NCC dispute/rate role and subsection (5) boundary.
Meaningful connectivity   Availability plus quality, affordability, device, skills/safety, relevance and
continuity.
Resilience   Prevent, withstand, reroute, restore and learn across real failure domains.
Ten traps to reject
Coverage equals subscription or use.
Fibre kilometres automatically mean connected people.
Strong signal proves adequate Internet capacity.
Two purchased links are physically diverse.
Open access means free or unlimited access.
An NCC licence replaces land and works approvals.
NCC has unlimited right-of-way jurisdiction.
A plan target is an achieved result.
The 2020-2025 plan is automatically current in 2026.
Every fibre cut is vandalism.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   126

Chapter 12
Numbering, portability and electronic addressing
A network needs consistent addresses as well as physical connections. Number administration
governs scarce resources, routing, portability and their efficient lifecycle.

12.1 Section 128 - the statutory engine
Section 128(1) vests NCC solely and exclusively with control, planning, administration, management
and assignment of numbering and electronic addressing for network services and applications
services. Each word matters.
Function   Regulatory meaning
Control   NCC is the authoritative sector custodian; incompatible private numbering
cannot govern the public network.
Planning   Design the structure, capacity, categories and future evolution before
individual grants.
Administration   Operate applications, records, fees, publications, coordination and routine
processes.
Management   Monitor efficiency, resolve conflicts, conserve resources and adapt the system
over time.
Assignment   Grant controlled use of a defined number, block, code or address to an
eligible person.
Section 128(2)
NCC must develop a numbering and electronic-addressing plan for network and applications
services, taking account of the plan that existed when the Act commenced. The continuity clause
prevents legal reform from casually making the live network unreachable.
Section 128(3) - what rules may cover
Different resources for different services.
Assignment and transfer of numbers and electronic addresses.
Use of assigned resources.
Portability of assigned resources.
Provider plans for assignment and reassignment to end users.
Fees for assignment and transfer, as determined by NCC.
Section 128(4)
NCC must make the plan available to the public, subject to a fee it decides. Public accessibility
supports predictability, interoperability and accountability.
Section 128 is not simply a power to issue phone numbers. It establishes an integrated
stewardship cycle from national architecture to end-user reassignment.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   127

12.2 Section 129 - delegation without abdication
NCC may delegate any or all Chapter functions to a person it chooses and may appoint a person or
organisation to manage an integrated public-number or electronic-address database. Delegation
enables specialist operation; it does not erase NCC's statutory accountability.
Section 129 element   Control implication
Delegation   Scope, duration, reporting, authority and revocation should be documented.
Integrated database manager   Must maintain availability, accuracy, security, audit and industry interfaces.
Commercial access   Commission or appointee provides non-discriminatory access on the same
terms it offers itself.
NCC direction   NCC may direct how the appointed person discharges the non-discrimination
obligation.
Operational governance
Service levels for uptime, transaction time, fault resolution and planned maintenance.
Data definitions, validation, reconciliation and correction authority.
Cybersecurity, privileged access, segregation of duties and breach response.
Business continuity, geographically appropriate recovery and tested restoration.
Transparent access onboarding and equivalent treatment of competitors.
Audit rights, change control, exit assistance and return/destruction of regulated data.
Conflict risk
A database operator with an affiliated retail business could favour itself through faster access, better
information or delayed competitor onboarding. Section 129(3) directly addresses this risk through
non-discriminatory commercial access.
Delegating database operation does not privatise the national numbering function or allow
the delegate to rewrite the plan beyond its authority.

12.3 The national numbering plan as a system
A numbering plan is the grammar that lets people and networks interpret digits consistently. It
allocates semantic space: some prefixes or lengths indicate a country, service, geography, network
function or special access route.
Concept   Explanation
Country code   International identifier assigned within the global E.164 framework; Nigeria
uses +234.
International prefix   Dialling method used to reach the international network; the plus sign
represents the appropriate access method in user interfaces.
National significant number   National destination digits interpreted after the country code.
Trunk prefix   Domestic dialling convention used where the plan requires it; not necessarily
part of the international-format number.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master
metadata.topic: 12.3 The national numbering plan as a system
metadata.section: 12.3 The national numbering plan as a system

chunks.content:
NCC Promotion Study Guide   128
Concept   Explanation
Prefix/range   Structured leading digits associated with a service or original allocation.
Subscriber number   Digits distinguishing a destination within the relevant range.
Closed and open plans
A closed plan generally uses a uniform national format without geographic dialling variation; an open
plan may use different local and national forms. The exam value is the distinction, not an unsupported
claim about a current format: quote Nigeria's precise current rules only from the controlled plan.
Plan expansion
Adding digits or changing prefixes affects switches, billing, lawful interception, emergency access,
directories, enterprise systems, advertising and international routing. A migration needs stakeholder
consultation, parallel acceptance where appropriate, public education, testing and a definite cutover.
Conservation
A mathematically large space can become operationally scarce through fragmentation, reserved
blocks, inefficient grants or incompatible legacy use. NCC must protect sufficient contiguous
resources for growth and new services.
+234 is Nigeria's country code; it is not an operator prefix and does not identify a
subscriber by itself.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master
metadata.topic: 12.3 The national numbering plan as a system
metadata.section: 12.3 The national numbering plan as a system

chunks.content:
12.4 Resource categories and short codes
Category   Purpose and principal control
Geographic/fixed   Addresses fixed services within the plan; location meaning and portability
depend on current rules.
Mobile   Public mobile destination; scale, routing, portability and lifecycle accuracy are
central.
Service/non-geographic   Represents a service class rather than a physical area; charging and
reachability must be clear.
Emergency/public interest   Memorable access requiring ubiquitous, reliable configuration and protection
from confusion.
Commercial short code   Convenient access to provider or content service; consent, price, ownership
and complaint controls apply.
Network/signalling code   Coordinates internal networks/functions rather than ordinary public dialling.
Machine/Internet of Things   May require large-scale or specialised lifecycle treatment; assignment must
remain plan-consistent.
Harmonisation
Historically, customers memorised different operator codes for the same basic function. NCC's
harmonised-short-code programme standardised common consumer functions across mobile
networks, reducing confusion and easing switching. The purpose and governance are more important
than reciting digits without verification.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   129
High-value verified set for final recall
The 2023 harmonisation materials identify common codes including 300 for call-centre/help-desk
access, 310 for balance, 311 for recharge, 312 for data plans, 323 for data balance, 305 to stop a
service, 996 for National Identification Number related functions, and 2442 for mobile-number
portability. Before the final freeze, compare the complete current NCC list and operator
implementation; do not infer a tariff merely from code length.
Governance questions
Is the code national, operator-specific, shared or exclusively assigned?
Which networks and technologies must reach it?
What tariff or free-access rule applies and how is it disclosed?
Who owns the service content and complaint duty?
What happens when an assignment ends or changes?
Harmonisation standardises access codes for common functions; it does not merge the
operators' underlying service platforms.

12.5 Assignment, utilisation and recovery
Stage   Control question
Application   Is the applicant licensed and is the resource necessary for the authorised
service?
Assessment   Does the request fit the plan, utilisation record, forecast and future capacity?
Decision   What block/code, purpose, conditions, fee, activation milestone and reporting
duty apply?
Activation   Has the grantee implemented routing and interoperability correctly?
Monitoring   Are utilisation, end-user assignment and returns accurate and efficient?
Variation/transfer   Is prior approval required and will continuity and competition be protected?
Withdrawal/recovery   What authority, breach/non-use evidence, notice, migration and consumer
safeguards apply?
Ownership misconception
Assignment normally gives a controlled right of use; it does not convert national numbering space into
permanent private property. Subscribers likewise receive service use and continuity protections, not
authority to sell plan resources independently of the provider and regulatory framework.
Utilisation arithmetic
Allocated capacity, provider inventory, provisioned numbers, active subscriptions, traffic-bearing
numbers, quarantined numbers and available numbers are different measures. A utilisation rate is
meaningless unless numerator, denominator, exclusions and date are stated.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   130
Hoarding versus readiness
Low utilisation may reflect inflated demand, but also rollout lead time, disaster recovery, quarantine or
a specialised service. NCC should test forecast accuracy, assignment age, activation and credible
pipeline before recovering resources.
Recovery risk
Premature recovery can make customers unreachable and disrupt authentication. Use notice, an
accurate affected-user count, migration, public communication and routing cleanup. Preserve
historical records after current assignment ends.
Efficient use is not maximum instantaneous occupancy. It is justified, plan-consistent use that
protects future capacity without undermining service continuity.

12.6 How number portability changes routing
Without portability, a prefix can indicate the original range holder and often guide routing. After a
subscriber ports, that visible prefix remains while the serving network changes. Networks therefore
need current portability information or an agreed routing mechanism.
Method   Meaning and risk
All-call query   Originating network consults portability data and routes directly to the current
recipient network; stale lookup produces failure or misrouting.
Onward routing   Call first reaches the original/donor context and is forwarded; adds
dependency and may be less efficient.
Query on release   Initial attempt receives a portability indication and a subsequent query
determines destination.
Central reference database   Authoritative port transaction/status information supports industry
synchronisation; participants still need correct local copies/configuration.
Porting actors
Actor   Core responsibility
Subscriber   Makes an authorised request and satisfies current validation requirements.
Recipient provider   Initiates and manages onboarding, communicates status and activates
service.
Donor provider   Validates only permitted grounds and releases the number without
anti-competitive obstruction.
Central operator/function   Coordinates transactions and authoritative data under regulated rules.
All networks   Update routing so calls and messages reach the current serving network.
NCC   Sets framework, monitors performance, resolves/escalates non-compliance
and protects competition/consumers.
The prefix may reveal the original allocation, not the present serving provider. Portability
separates visible number identity from current network location.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   131

12.7 Mobile number portability process and controls
Nigeria's Mobile Number Portability Regulations 2014 provide the formal regulatory framework.
Operational business rules and port-order handling processes supply implementation detail. Do not
turn an old process time or rejection code into timeless law without checking the current instrument.
Phase   Evidence and control
Request   Correct number, subscriber authority, recipient channel, timestamp and
informed consent.
Validation   Permitted identity/account checks; no invented donor obstruction or retention
pressure.
Authorisation   Secure confirmation protects against fraudulent port-out while remaining
accessible to legitimate users.
Central processing   Unique order, consistent state, timestamps, rejection reason and
retry/cancellation control.
Activation   Recipient service works; donor service ceases at the coordinated point; no
avoidable dual control.
Routing convergence   Other networks receive/apply updated destination data and complete
cross-network tests.
Closure/redress   Subscriber notification, record retention, failure remedy, complaint and
performance reporting.
Competition purpose
Portability lowers the switching cost created by losing a familiar number. It can discipline quality and
price by making exit easier, but only when the process is predictable, fraud-resistant and not
burdened by artificial rejection.
Donor conduct
The donor may protect valid obligations only through permitted rules. It should not use confidential
port information for aggressive retention, delay, false debt claims or degradation. The recipient must
not submit unauthorised or misleading requests.
Port history
A number can port more than once. Current routing state and historical transaction trail should be
distinct. Retaining history supports audit and fraud investigation; presenting obsolete donor data as
current creates harm.
A good MNP regime balances three outcomes: easy legitimate switching, accurate industry routing
and strong protection against unauthorised transfer.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master
metadata.topic: 12.7 Mobile number portability process and controls

chunks.content:
12.8 Failure diagnosis and performance measurement
Symptom   Likely test path
Calls from one network fail after port   Check that network's portability lookup, route tables and signalling against the
central state.
All incoming traffic fails; outgoing
works
Confirm recipient activation, routing publication and destination acceptance.
Calls still reach former provider   Identify stale local data, onward-routing configuration or incomplete port
closure.
SMS works but voice fails   Separate service routes, interconnection and platform configuration.
Port repeatedly rejected   Examine exact permitted reason, evidence, timestamps and donor/recipient
behaviour.
Unexpected long outage   Reconstruct order state, cutover, routing propagation, fault escalation and
consumer updates.
Key performance measures
Requests received, completed, rejected, cancelled and failed by provider and reason.
End-to-end completion time using a consistent start and stop definition.
Service interruption during cutover and time to routing convergence.
Repeat submissions and unresolved database mismatches.
Complaints, unauthorised ports, restoration time and recurrence.
Availability, response time, recovery and reconciliation of central/local systems.
Denominator discipline
A high rejection count can reflect higher demand rather than worse behaviour. Compare rates using
valid requests as denominator, distinguish user cancellation from provider rejection, and analyse
reasons. Average completion time can conceal severe tails; use distributions and overdue cases.
Evidence hierarchy
A subscriber screenshot proves a symptom, not necessarily root cause. Combine port-order logs,
central status, local database timestamps, signalling traces, activation records, customer
communications and network tests.
Completed in the central database does not by itself prove the subscriber has working
end-to-end service.

12.9 Electronic addressing beyond telephone numbers
The Act deliberately covers numbering and electronic addressing. This future-facing language
permits coordinated treatment of network or applications-service addresses that may not be ordinary
dialled telephone numbers.
Identifier/address   Regulatory distinction
Telephone number   Public routable service address under the national numbering plan.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   133
Identifier/address   Regulatory distinction
Internet Protocol address   Logical network address allocated through the global/regional
Internet-number-resource system; not simply assigned by NCC as a phone
number.
Domain name   Human-readable name resolved through the Domain Name System;
governance involves registries, registrars and global/national structures.
Electronic mail address   Application identifier built from a local part and domain; not proof of legal
identity.
Uniform Resource Locator   Location/reference for an Internet resource, incorporating scheme and host;
can change or redirect.
Network/signalling identifier   Technical code used for network coordination; may be regulated even though
consumers never dial it.
Avoid jurisdictional overreach
Section 128 gives wide sector authority, but global Internet identifiers have their own institutional
allocation and governance systems. A strong answer explains coordination and statutory purpose
without asserting that NCC unilaterally controls every global Internet address.
Address scarcity and transition
Internet Protocol version 4 scarcity encouraged conservation, transfer markets and address sharing;
Internet Protocol version 6 expands address space but requires compatible networks, security,
monitoring and dual-stack transition. Neither version is a telephone-number plan.
Identity versus address
An address indicates where or how to reach a service; it may not establish the human's legal identity.
Dynamic reassignment, shared addresses, forwarding and spoofing all weaken simplistic identity
inference.
Electronic addressing is broader than telephone numbering, but similarity of function does
not make every identifier subject to identical institutions and rules.

12.10 Fraud, privacy and lifecycle assurance
Threat   What actually changes
SIM swap/replacement fraud   Subscriber credentials or SIM profile changes while the public number can
remain with the same provider.
Port-out fraud   Serving provider changes without valid subscriber authority.
Number spoofing   Displayed calling identity is falsified; the attacker need not control the actual
number.
Recycling harm   A lawfully reassigned number remains linked to the former holder's third-party
accounts.
Range misuse   Numbers are used outside assigned purpose or without authority.
Call masking/refiling   Traffic identity or origin is manipulated, affecting fraud detection, charging or
compliance.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   134
Lifecycle assurance
Authenticate high-risk changes using proportionate independent evidence.
Notify the existing trusted channel before or promptly after a sensitive change where safe.
Apply maker-checker approval and exception monitoring.
Publish swap, churn, port and reassignment status to authorised systems promptly.
Use quarantine before reissue and remove obsolete current identity links.
Retain lawful historical attribution separately for investigation and accountability.
Give consumers rapid containment and restoration channels that do not depend solely on the
compromised SIM.
Privacy controls
Numbering databases can expose contact, network and transaction history. Limit access by purpose
and role; minimise returned data; encrypt and log; set retention; investigate unusual queries; and
distinguish public routing information from confidential subscriber data.
Cross-sector reliance
Banks and platforms often use numbers for authentication. NCC can improve telecommunications
lifecycle signals, but relying institutions remain responsible for their own identity and transaction
controls. A normal number status is not proof that the presenter is the lawful account owner.
Preserve two truths at once: obsolete current links must be removed to protect the new holder,
while historical records must remain available under lawful access.

12.11 Regulatory system and data model
Record   Essential fields
Plan resource   Category, parent range, length, status, reservation and version/effective date.
Assignment   Holder, licence, purpose, decision, conditions, fee, effective/expiry date and
authoriser.
Utilisation return   Period, allocated/provisioned/active/quarantine/free counts, definition and
certification.
Port transaction   Number, donor, recipient, request/state timestamps, reason and audit trail.
Routing status   Authoritative current destination, publication/version and participant
acknowledgements.
Short-code service   Holder, purpose, tariff, networks, content provider, consumer contacts and
status.
Case/enforcement   Complaint, evidence, affected records, direction/remedy, review and verified
closure.
Control architecture
No assignment outside an active licence and approved service scope.
No overlapping active resources unless the plan explicitly defines shared use.
Maker-checker for assignment, transfer, recovery and manual port correction.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   135
Immutable audit of before/after value, actor, authority, reason and time.
Automated reconciliation between NCC register, central database and operator returns.
Role-based access, privileged-session monitoring and periodic entitlement review.
Tested backup and recovery with recovery-time and recovery-point objectives.
Versioned public plan and machine-readable industry distribution.
System change
Plan or interface changes need impact analysis, sandbox testing, conformance cases, participant
certification, rollback and post-change monitoring. A central upgrade that works internally can still fail
if operator adapters interpret the schema differently.
Internal NCC coordination
Technical, licensing, legal, consumer, competition, finance, cybersecurity and information-technology
functions contribute different evidence. One case owner should coordinate them so the licensee
receives a coherent decision rather than conflicting departmental instructions.
A dashboard can display consistent-looking totals from inconsistent definitions. Data
lineage and reconciliation come before visualisation.

12.12 Applied level 10 scenarios
Scenario 1 - Large allocation request
Confirm licence and service; calculate current utilisation using controlled definitions; test forecast,
rollout and quarantine; consider a staged block; impose activation/reporting conditions; preserve
future plan space and record reasons.
Scenario 2 - Emergency short code fails on one network
Treat as urgent public-safety risk. Verify authoritative assignment, test technologies/locations, inspect
translations and interconnection, direct temporary restoration, publish safe alternatives where
necessary, then investigate compliance and recurrence.
Scenario 3 - Port is centrally complete but calls fail
Compare authoritative destination with each network's local version and query logs; use signalling
traces; correct stale routes; test voice and messaging from all networks; measure outage and remedy
the subscriber.
Scenario 4 - Donor rejects for alleged debt
Check whether the current regulations/business rules permit that reason and what evidence exists.
Separate debt recovery from portability unless the operative rule lawfully connects them; identify
systematic retention behaviour.
Scenario 5 - Recycled number receives bank alerts
Protect both users: verify assignment/quarantine, avoid disclosing former-holder identity, alert the
relying institution lawfully, correct lifecycle signals and assess whether authentication relied
improperly on number possession.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   136
Scenario 6 - Database delegate favours affiliate
Compare access terms, onboarding time, outage priority, data quality and information flow. Apply
section 129(3)'s same-terms non-discrimination and direct corrective conduct under subsection (4).
Scenario 7 - New digital service requests millions of numbers
Challenge whether individual public numbers are technically necessary. Consider machine identifiers,
shared addressing or another plan-consistent architecture; evaluate scale, routing, lifecycle, fraud
and future capacity before assignment.
Scenario 8 - Misleading caller identity
Do not assume the displayed number originated the call. Preserve signalling and interconnect
records, trace the ingress path, distinguish spoofing from subscriber misuse, coordinate enforcement
and protect the impersonated holder.
MODEL ANSWER FORMULA
Define the resource   →   cite section 128/129 or current instrument   →   establish authoritative
plan/database state   →   trace routing and lifecycle   →   identify competent actors   →   protect
consumer/competition   →   direct correction and verify convergence.
Do not confuse   Correct distinction
Number/spectrum   Logical routable address / physical radio-frequency resource.
Assignment/ownership   Regulated right of use / proprietary title.
Allocation/activation   NCC grant / network implementation.
Active subscription/person   Service record meeting activity rule / unique human being.
Port/SIM replacement   Change of provider / change of SIM or profile.
Original range holder/current network   Initial allocation / present serving provider after port.
Central completion/end-to-end
service
Database state / actual routing, activation and user reachability.
Address/identity   Reachability reference / proof of who the person is.
Current-status control
Primary anchors are NCA 2003 sections 128-129 and the Mobile Number Portability Regulations
2014. The National Numbering Plan, assignment procedures, harmonised short-code implementation
and MNP business/process rules must be checked in their latest official editions before final freeze.
The 2014 date remains the verified regulation date as recorded in the cited edition; a newer webpage
or industry practice must not be presented as repeal without instrument-level evidence.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   137

Chapter 13
Subscriber registration and telecommunications
identity
A telephone number, a subscription, a person and a device are different objects. This chapter first
establishes the identities, then follows registration, activation, changes, recycling and risk signals.

13.1 Four identifiers, four jobs
Stop calling everything a SIM number
Identifier   What it identifies   What it does not prove
Mobile Subscriber Integrated
Services Digital Network
Number (MSISDN)
The publicly reachable mobile service
number.
The human identity, physical SIM or
device on its own.
International Mobile
Subscriber Identity (IMSI)
A subscription identity used by mobile
networks for authentication and mobility
functions.
The device hardware or public dialling
number by itself.
Integrated Circuit Card
Identifier (ICCID)
The particular SIM card or embedded
profile container issued through the
supply chain.
The current user or handset.
International Mobile
Equipment Identity (IMEI)
The mobile equipment or handset identity.   The subscriber's entitlement to use the
service.
Why separation matters
A subscriber can replace a damaged SIM and retain the same public number: the card identifier
changes while the service number remains. A person can move the SIM into another handset: the
equipment identity changes while subscriber and service identities may remain. A port can keep the
public number while network-serving relationships change. Investigation therefore needs a
time-stamped relationship among identifiers, not one field treated as permanent truth.
Embedded SIM does not abolish identity control
An embedded Subscriber Identity Module can download and manage operator profiles without
inserting a removable plastic card. The form factor changes; the regulator still needs secure
provisioning, authorised profile lifecycle, subscriber registration, device compatibility, switching and
consumer protection.
Privacy and proportionality
These identifiers can reveal sensitive relationships and activity. Access should be purpose-limited,
role-based, logged and retained only as lawfully required. Staff should not export complete datasets
when a targeted query will answer the regulatory question.
A phone number identifies a reachable service, not conclusively the natural person holding
the handset at a particular moment.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   138

13.2 The governing implementation edition
The Registration of Communications Subscribers Regulations 2022 remain the regulatory anchor for
the August 2026 Business Rules. The latter record first issuance in August 2022, first amendment in
April 2024 and second amendment in August 2026. The Rules are an implementation layer, not a
new principal regulation merely because their publication carries 2026. Source: NCC, Business Rules
for Registration of Communications Subscribers Regulations, document history and introduction,
consulted 22 September 2026.

13.3 Subscriber registration and NIN
The regulatory objective
Subscriber registration connects a communications service to a sufficiently verified person or
authorised organisation. National Identification Number integration strengthens the identity anchor by
checking subscriber information against the national identity system. The objective is accountable
access and trustworthy records, not collection for its own sake.
Individual transaction
The customer presents the required identity information and requests service.
The communications service provider obtains and verifies the National Identification Number through
the prescribed interface.
Biometric or facial checks establish that the present person corresponds to the identity record.
Consent and lawful-use notices govern copying or using foundational information for the service
record.
Registration data and a live image are captured or aligned as required.
The mobile number and subscription are linked to the verified record.
Activation occurs only when the applicable controls succeed.
The provider retains evidence and supplies required regulatory records securely.
Verification is not the same as data duplication
Verification answers whether a claim matches an authoritative source. Copying creates another
stored dataset with its own accuracy, access, security and retention risks. The process should
minimise unnecessary duplication while preserving the functional registration record and audit
evidence required by law.
A failed check is a case, not a licence to improvise
Mismatch, unavailable service, poor biometric capture or suspected impersonation should trigger
defined exception handling. Agents must not substitute another person's identity, edit authoritative
fields informally or bypass activation controls to meet sales targets.
Identity assurance is a chain. A strong national identity database cannot compensate for weak
agent authentication, poor capture, insecure transfer or unauthorised post-verification changes.

13.4 Who does what: NCC, NIMC, CSP and subscriber
The 2026 Rules distribute responsibility. They should not be reduced to the slogan 'link NIN to SIM'.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master

metadata.section: 13.4 Who does what: NCC, NIMC, CSP and subscriber

chunks.content:
NCC Promotion Study Guide   139
Actor   Core role in the registration chain
NCC   Regulates the process, issues the governing framework, approves specified
methods and supervises compliance.
National Identity Management
Commission
Maintains the National Identity Database and performs identity verification
through its approved verification service.
Communications service provider   Captures or receives required registration information, invokes verification,
manages activation and lifecycle controls, keeps records and protects data
within its obligations.
Subscriber   Provides valid information, presents the required identity basis, gives
applicable consent and regularises identity data where necessary.
Agent/dealer   Performs authorised capture or service functions within the provider's
controlled framework; agency does not erase provider accountability.
The ordinary-language flow
The person seeks a subscription or another covered transaction.
Required live capture or approved information is collected through an authorised channel.
The claimed identity is checked against the National Identity Database through the approved
verification service.
The subscriber record must align with the verified identity data; identity corrections are first made at
the authoritative identity source.
Activation occurs only after the required verification and registration conditions are satisfied.
The resulting subscriber-number relationship remains subject to consent, security, lifecycle, churn
and recycling controls.
Important responsibility distinction
The Rules describe subscriber registration as a regulatory function under the Commission's authority
while communications service providers execute specified operational processes. In an exam
answer, avoid converting institutional authority into the false claim that NCC staff personally capture
every subscriber.
NIN rule
The National Identification Number is the ordinary identity basis for subscriber activation and
mobile-number portability, subject to the special treatment provided for exempt categories of foreign
nationals. The verification result, not the mere typing of digits, is what connects the claim to an
authoritative identity record.
Accountability, database authority and operational execution are related but different roles.

13.5 Activation, service events and data alignment
Activation is a controlled event, not simply the physical insertion of a Subscriber Identity Module into a
handset.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master
metadata.topic: 13.5 Activation, service events and data alignment
metadata.section: 13.5 Activation, service events and data alignment

chunks.content:
NCC Promotion Study Guide   140
Rule area   2026 teaching position
Before activation   A new line must not receive ordinary service before activation; the limited
ability to receive registration-related text messages does not equal full
service.
Identity alignment   The communications-provider record must align with verified National Identity
Database information. Changes to identity data should first be regularised at
the authoritative identity database.
Verification channel   The provider uses the approved NIMC verification service rather than treating
a photocopy or unverified number as sufficient proof.
Revenue-generating event   The rules require a revenue-generating event within 48 hours and a further
event by 96 hours, linking activation to evidence of genuine use.
BVN-generated NIN   Where the National Identification Number is flagged as generated through the
Bank Verification Number pathway, regularisation requirements must be
satisfied.
Line limits   The total number of lines permitted is determined by the Commission from
time to time; do not freeze a variable administrative limit into a permanent
teaching rule.
Why the revenue-generating-event control exists
It provides a lifecycle signal after activation. It helps distinguish a newly activated line entering
genuine use from a stockpiled, improperly activated or inactive subscription. It is one control among
many and should not be described as conclusive proof of the subscriber's identity.
Scenario
A provider captures a face and National Identification Number but activates the line before receiving
successful identity verification. Even if the identity later proves genuine, the sequence defeats the
control: verification is a precondition, not a post-activation tidy-up.
Possession of a NIN is not the same as successful NIMC verification, and successful
verification is not the same as completion of every activation control.

metadata.title: NCC_Study_Guide_Restructured_Master
metadata.topic: 13.5 Activation, service events and data alignment
metadata.section: 13.5 Activation, service events and data alignment

chunks.content:
13.6 Biometrics, liveness, consent and privacy
The 2026 Rules allow biometric methods approved by the Commission, including facial or fingerprint
processes, and include detailed controls for live capture and facial-image quality. The objective is not
to collect more data for its own sake; it is to reduce impersonation, replay, proxy capture and record
mismatch.
Control   Purpose
Live image/fingerprint capture   Binds the transaction to a present person and makes reuse of stored artefacts
harder.
Liveness and image-quality testing   Tests whether the image is suitable and plausibly captured from a live subject
rather than a photograph or screen.
NIMC verification   Compares the claimed identity with the authoritative identity record.
Consent   Authorises specified harmonisation, update or corporate-management
actions; it must be attributable and appropriately recorded.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   141
Control   Purpose
Data minimisation and security   Limits unnecessary exposure while preserving evidence required for
compliance.
Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023   Provides the broader current data-protection framework alongside
sector-specific consumer and registration controls.
Recognised consent channels
The Rules contemplate evidence through channels such as text message, web, email or physical
documentation. The correct question is not merely 'Was a box ticked?' but whether the consent was
informed, attributable, recorded, appropriately scoped and capable of audit.
A useful four-question test
Identity: whose consent is it?
Intention: what action was authorised?
Integrity: can the record be altered or replayed without detection?
Accountability: can the provider demonstrate the event and its scope later?
Security reasoning
Biometrics are powerful because they are difficult to substitute, but that also increases harm if
compromised. They require strong access control, encryption, retention discipline, audit trails,
incident response and lawful-purpose limitation.
Biometric strength and privacy risk rise together; the answer is governed processing, not
indiscriminate collection.

13.7 Complex subscriber categories
Corporate subscriptions
A company cannot present a face or fingerprint. The process must prove the organisation's legal
existence, the authority of a designated representative and the association of individual users with
lines. The applicable rules use responsible corporate roles and secondary-user validation so a large
pool of lines is not hidden behind one unaccountable identity.
Control layer   Question
Entity   Does the organisation exist and do its documents match authoritative
records?
Authority   Who may request, change, replace or terminate lines for the organisation?
Primary responsible person   Whose verified identity anchors administration of the account?
Secondary users   Which natural person uses each line where the rules require association?
Change management   How are leavers, reassignment, lost devices and new administrators
updated?
Audit   Can the provider reconstruct who authorised each lifecycle event?

NCC Promotion Study Guide   142
Foreigners and visitors
A lawful user may not possess the same Nigerian identity credentials as a citizen or long-term
resident. Rules therefore distinguish relevant categories and alternative documents or activation
conditions. The principle is equivalent assurance through the prescribed route, not either exclusion or
an uncontrolled exemption.
Minors, dependants and assisted registration
Where special arrangements apply, the record must distinguish the actual service user from the
responsible adult or representative. Assistance must not erase consent, accountability or
safeguarding. Staff should consult the operative rule rather than assume a general age or proxy rule.
Machine-to-machine and Internet-of-Things services
A sensor has no personal biography, but the entity deploying and controlling it is accountable.
Registration should connect the resource to the licensed service, responsible organisation, device
estate, purpose and lifecycle. High-volume machine deployments demand bulk controls without
sacrificing traceability.
Corporate registration does not mean placing every line under a director's name and
forgetting the users. Entity authority and line-level accountability are separate controls.

13.8 CORPORATE SUBSCRIPTIONS, TELECOM MASTERS AND
IoT/M2M
Corporate registration is not anonymous bulk activation. The 2026 framework uses accountable
natural-person roles to govern subscriptions held for an organisation.
Concept   Meaning
Primary Telecom Master   The principal verified natural person authorised to manage relevant corporate
subscription matters.
Secondary Telecom Master   An additional authorised role where used; it supports operations but does not
erase the Primary Telecom Master's accountability.
Corporate record   Connects the legal organisation, its authorised representatives and the lines
or profiles managed for it.
Internet of Things /
machine-to-machine profile
A non-ordinary-user profile linked to an accountable corporate master and
restricted to its approved technical purpose.
Point-to-point / URL-specific data
restriction
Constrains a machine profile so it communicates only with defined endpoints
or services rather than behaving as an unrestricted consumer subscription.
Why a natural person remains necessary
A company can own subscriptions, but accountability must reach a verifiable person who can
authorise changes, receive notices and answer for lifecycle actions. The person is not thereby treated
as the beneficial owner of every line; the role is one of controlled authority.
IoT example
A utility deploys connected meters. Each embedded profile is not used for ordinary voice and open
Internet access. The profiles are linked to the corporate registration structure, configured for
approved endpoints and monitored for anomalies. This combines identity accountability with
technical-purpose restriction.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   143
Distinctions that must survive
Corporate ownership is not personal ownership.
A Telecom Master is not automatically the end-user of every corporate line.
An Internet-of-Things profile is not exempt from accountability merely because no person speaks
through it.
Subscriber registration does not replace equipment type approval or device-status management.
'No human user' does not mean 'no accountable subscriber relationship'.

13.9 The number lifecycle
A number changes state
A number can be reserved, allocated, activated, used, suspended, barred, disconnected,
quarantined, recycled and reassigned. Subscriber, operator and third-party systems must understand
these changes. A database that stores only 'active' or 'inactive' cannot represent the risk.
State   Meaning   Control concern
Active   Provisioned for a current service.   Correct identity, lawful use and current
routing.
Suspended or barred   Use is restricted while the relationship or
investigation may continue.
Reason, authority, notice and restoration.
Disconnected   Service relationship has ended.   Stop charging, cease routing and begin
controlled lifecycle.
Quarantine   Number is withheld before possible reuse.   Reduce residual calls, messages and
stale-account risk.
Recycled or reassigned   Number is issued to a different
subscriber.
Remove old linkage and establish new
identity.
Why recycling is necessary
Permanently locking every disconnected number would eventually waste plan capacity. Recycling
returns resources to productive use. But time alone cannot cleanse a number: the operator must
remove prior identity links, update required systems, retain lawful history separately and create a
clean new registration.
Why quarantine helps but is not magic
A holding period allows traffic and stale associations to decline, yet banks, social platforms and
acquaintances may retain a number for years. The safe answer combines quarantine, cross-system
status signals, consumer education and stronger authentication by relying organisations.
Historical truth must remain auditable
Purging the previous identity from the current assignment does not mean destroying every lawful
historical record. Systems should separate current ownership or use from time-bounded history so
investigations can reconstruct who held the number on a relevant date without presenting the former
subscriber as the present one.
The core data model is temporal: which identity, SIM, device, operator and status were linked to
this number at this specific time?
NCC Promotion Study Guide   144

13.10 Mobile number portability under the 2026 registration layer
The August 2026 Rules integrate National Identification Number verification into mobile-number
portability while recognising the Mobile Number Portability Regulations and Business Rules 2014 as
the specialist portability framework.
Layer   Question answered
Subscriber-registration rules 2026   How identity, consent and registration integrity are established for the porting
subscriber.
MNP Regulations/Business Rules
2014
How the number is ported, including roles, process and specialist portability
controls.
Numbering framework   What the number represents and how the national numbering resource is
governed.
Recipient network   The network to which the subscriber ports.
Donor network   The network from which the subscriber ports.
Central portability systems   How routing and portability records are coordinated across providers.
Why both layers matter
Portability preserves a number while changing the serving network. That creates impersonation and
unauthorised-port risk. Identity verification protects the person-number relationship; specialist
portability rules govern the network transfer. Neither layer makes the other redundant.
Scenario
A fraudster knows a victim's number and possesses biographical details but cannot complete
compliant live capture and authoritative identity verification. The registration layer should stop the
identity substitution before the portability process can validly transfer control.
Model conclusion
The Commission's regulatory objective is not merely administrative accuracy. Secure portability
protects consumer choice and competition without sacrificing identity integrity, network trust or lawful
traceability.
NIN verification does not itself complete a port; it satisfies an identity condition within the
wider MNP process.
