15.18 Selected metric contexts
Context   Verified target/status
2G busy-hour call setup success, cell
level
At least 98.50 percent; specified exception consideration.
2G busy-hour dropped-call rate, cell
level
At most 1.00 percent; specified exception consideration.
4G drive-test user throughput   At least 20 megabits per second downlink and 5 megabits per second uplink.
Terrestrial Internet service provider
packet loss
At most 0.50 percent.
Colocation power availability   At least 99.50 percent terminal sites and 99.80 percent hub sites.
Colocation Mean Time to Repair   At most 2.5 hours.
The published Business Rules record July 2024 as Version 1 and August 2026 as Version 2. A
numerical target must stay attached to the service, technology, aggregation, measurement method
and compliance or monitoring label used by that edition. Source: NCC, Quality of Service Business
Rules, August 2026, document history and relevant tables.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   180

Chapter 16
Consumer protection, complaints and redress
Quality measurement describes performance. Consumer protection considers the person affected:
information, consent, billing, access, complaint handling, correction and systemic prevention.

16.1 Statutory foundation - section 104
Section 104 imposes three connected obligations on every service provider in relation to its specific
services.
Duty   Meaning
Meet minimum quality standards   Comply with standards NCC specifies and publishes; this links consumer
protection to measurable service performance.
Deal reasonably with consumers   Exercise contractual and operational power fairly, proportionately,
transparently and without avoidable hardship.
Adequately address complaints   Provide an effective first-level process capable of receiving, tracking,
investigating and resolving issues.
Reasonableness is contextual
A provider may have a contractual power to suspend service, but its use can still be unreasonable if
the bill is genuinely disputed, notice was defective, the provider's own system caused the error, or
reconnection is needlessly delayed. Ask what the provider knew, what it could practically do and how
serious the consumer impact was.
Quality is not only engineering
Network indicators matter, but the consumer receives an end-to-end service including activation, tariff
disclosure, billing, support, fault repair and communication. A radio network can meet a technical
average while an individual suffers an unresolved provisioning or billing failure.
Adequacy
A complaint channel is not adequate merely because it exists. Consumers must be able to reach it;
receive a reference; explain the problem; supply evidence safely; obtain status; understand the
decision; and escalate an unresolved matter.
Relationship with section 4
NCC's broader functions include protecting and promoting consumer interests against unfair
practices and resolving complaints and objections. Chapter VII turns that mandate into specific
provider duties and complaint architecture.
Section 104 is outcome-oriented. It connects technical quality, fair conduct and operational
complaint handling instead of treating them as separate silos.

16.2 Section 105 - two-level complaint resolution
Section 105(1) allows NCC to use its powers under the Act to resolve consumer complaints
concerning customer service and consumer protection, including quality of service and failure to
comply with a consumer code.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   181
Operator first
Under section 105(2), the consumer must first exhaust the licensee's dispute-resolution procedure
without resolution before presenting the complaint to NCC. This creates a two-level system: provider
first-level support; NCC second-level support and regulatory oversight.
Level   Responsibility
Service provider   Receive complaint, issue ticket/reference, preserve records, investigate,
remedy and communicate within the applicable service level.
Consumer   Use the official provider channel, explain accurately, keep the ticket and
relevant evidence, and cooperate with reasonable verification.
NCC   Confirm threshold, protect urgent interests, obtain evidence, mediate or
determine within its powers, require remedy and identify systemic breach.
Why exhaustion exists
The provider controls the immediate operational systems and can often resolve fastest.
It creates a traceable record of the allegation and provider response.
NCC resources can focus on unresolved, repeated or regulatory-significant matters.
Complaint data reveals whether first-level systems are effective.
Exhaustion is not a trapdoor
The rule should not be administered mechanically where provider channels are unavailable, refuse to
issue a ticket, the matter is urgent, or delay risks serious continuing harm. The applicable instrument
and facts determine the lawful treatment; the file should explain any exception or interim protective
step.
Alternative dispute resolution
NCC may establish complaint procedures and, at its discretion, alternative dispute-resolution
processes. Mediation can secure practical resolution, but systemic regulatory breaches may still
require enforcement even after the individual settles.
Operator-first handling does not deprive NCC of oversight, and settlement of one bill does
not automatically resolve a wider pattern of unlawful charging.

16.3 Section 106 and the consumer code
Section 106 permits NCC to designate an industry consumer forum to prepare a code, or require
licensees to prepare individual codes. In either case, prior NCC approval and ratification are required.
Mandatory code concern   Practical expression
Reasonably meeting consumer
requirements
Accessible products, information and support reflecting actual user needs.
Complaint and dispute handling   Clear procedure, inexpensive non-court arbitration and compensation for code
breach.
Consumer-information protection   Purpose limitation, security, controlled disclosure and lawful retention.
Further recourse   Escalation beyond provider process, with specific refund and compensation
arrangements.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   182
Mandatory code concern   Practical expression
Service information   Terms, rates, performance and material limitations before commitment.
Provisioning and repair   Order progress, appointment, fault diagnosis, restoration and communication.
Advertising/representation   Claims must be accurate, supportable and not omit material conditions.
Charging/billing/credit   Accurate records, understandable bills, dispute process and fair collection.
Publication and review
The Act requires publication after ratification, newspaper notice and annual review and ratification
before publication. The code is therefore intended to remain visible and responsive, not an internal
manual consumers cannot inspect.
Current instrument
NCC's official regulations register lists the Consumer Code of Practice Regulations 2024 as published
and operative. It supersedes the older teaching focus on the 2007/2006-era framework. Historical
codes remain useful for chronology, but current exam emphasis belongs on the 2024 Regulations
unless a later instrument is officially verified.
General and individual codes
The general framework sets minimum sector expectations. A licensee's individual code explains how
it will meet them for its services and cannot lawfully dilute the general standard.
A provider-written code is not self-approving. Section 106 expressly requires prior NCC
approval and ratification.

16.4 Consumer rights and responsibilities
Consumer right   What it requires
Choice   Ability to compare lawful alternatives without deceptive lock-in or concealed
conditions.
Accurate information   Clear price, validity, renewal, speed/performance limits and material
exclusions.
Correct billing   Charges supported by authorised tariff, consent, usage and accurate records.
Quality service   Performance meeting applicable regulatory and contractual standards.
Be heard   Accessible complaint channel, reference, fair investigation and reasoned
communication.
Redress   Correction, restoration, refund, compensation or other suitable remedy where
established.
Privacy and security   Reasonable protection and lawful handling of consumer information.
Safety and accessibility   Safe equipment/service and reasonable access for persons with disabilities or
other barriers.
Consumer responsibilities
Provide accurate registration and complaint information.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   183
Protect devices, passwords, personal identification numbers and one-time passwords.
Read material plan conditions and use official provider channels.
Pay valid undisputed charges and raise errors promptly.
Keep ticket numbers, messages, receipts and relevant records.
Do not misuse emergency, complaint or network services.
Cooperate with proportionate troubleshooting without surrendering unnecessary personal
information.
Rights are not blamed away
Consumer education helps prevent harm but does not excuse inaccurate billing, hidden terms or
weak security. Conversely, a consumer's allegation is not automatically proof. Fair protection tests
evidence and responsibility on both sides.
Vulnerable consumers
Age, disability, language, literacy, poverty, displacement or emergency can increase harm or make
ordinary channels inaccessible. Reasonable support may include accessible formats, authorised
representation, multiple channels, simplified explanations and priority treatment where service is
critical.
Consumer responsibility supports informed use; it must never be converted into a blanket defence
for provider non-compliance.

16.5 Consumer obligations
Rights do not remove responsibility
The General Code also addresses consumer obligations. Consumers should pay valid undisputed
charges, use services lawfully, protect equipment and credentials, provide accurate information,
permit reasonable authorised access where applicable, avoid network harm and follow lawful service
terms.
Consumer duty   Boundary
Pay valid charges   A disputed or erroneous amount still requires the applicable dispute process;
the provider cannot assume every complaint avoids payment.
Protect credentials   Provider remains responsible for secure processes and cannot shift all fraud
risk to the consumer.
Provide accurate information   Licensee must still verify and protect information under applicable rules.
Use service lawfully   Enforcement, restriction and termination need lawful authority and fair
process.
Permit necessary access   Access should be authorised, identified, scheduled and limited to legitimate
purpose.
Avoid resale without authority   A retail subscription does not automatically authorise licensed resale activity.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   184
Shared responsibility is not equal responsibility
The party controlling a system is usually better placed to prevent a technical harm. A consumer may
protect a password, but cannot secure the operator's agent portal. The licensee may educate about
phishing, but the bank controls its authentication design. Good analysis allocates each control to the
actor capable and legally required to perform it.
Terms must remain fair and lawful
A contract cannot eliminate statutory protection merely by stating that all failures are at the
subscriber's risk. Terms should be clear, consistent with the Regulations and not used to justify
misleading advertising, inaccurate billing or refusal to investigate.
Consumer protection does not mean the consumer always wins. NCC must determine valid
entitlement, facts and responsibility fairly.

16.6 Information before contract
Information must support a real decision
A consumer needs more than a product name and headline price. Material information includes what
the service does, where it is available, eligibility, activation, tariff, recurring charges, data or time
limits, quality limitations, equipment needs, renewal, termination, complaint channels and any fair-use
or roaming condition.
Information test   Question
Accuracy   Is the statement factually correct and current?
Completeness   Would omission of a condition change a reasonable consumer's decision?
Clarity   Can the intended audience understand the language and presentation?
Prominence   Are important limitations visible rather than hidden in a link or tiny print?
Timing   Was the information supplied before commitment or deduction?
Accessibility   Can consumers with disabilities or special needs obtain it in usable form?
Consistency   Do advert, website, agent script, contract and billing system agree?
Availability claims
A service described as available nationally may depend on coverage, technology, device capability or
location. The provider should state material constraints. A map is an estimate and should explain its
assumptions; it does not override the consumer's right to complain where actual service or
representation is misleading.
Contract change
Material changes to price, validity, benefits or billing require the notice and consent treatment
prescribed by applicable rules. A system notification should identify what changes, when, why, the
consumer's choices and where to obtain help. A vague 'terms updated' message does not
necessarily create informed choice.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   185
Sales agents
The licensee remains accountable for authorised agents and channels. Commission incentives can
encourage omission or mis-selling, so scripts, training, monitoring, mystery shopping, complaints and
sanctions should be controlled.
Disclosure is not adequate merely because the information exists somewhere. It must be
timely, clear, accessible and sufficiently prominent for the decision.

16.7 Complaint intake, triage and evidence
Intake field   Why it matters
Complainant/contact   Authenticate safely and maintain a usable communication route.
Affected service/account   Identify the correct legal subscriber, number, product and provider.
Provider ticket   Shows first-level reporting, timestamps and response history.
Problem statement   Separate symptom, requested remedy and alleged breach.
Time/location   Correlate network, billing, provisioning or security records.
Financial impact   Quantify disputed charge, loss, refund or compensation issue.
Evidence   Bills, messages, screenshots, contract, usage records and correspondence.
Risk flags   Safety, identity compromise, vulnerable person, widespread outage or
ongoing loss.
Triage
Classify urgency, subject, jurisdiction, first-level status, limitation/retention risk and possible systemic
impact. A stolen identity or emergency-service failure cannot sit in the same ordinary queue as a
minor information request.
Evidence is issue-specific
Allegation   Useful evidence
Wrong charge   Approved tariff, consent, event record, bundle state, bill and reversal.
Data depletion   Bundle purchase, device/session records, hotspot/sharing, application usage
and rating logs.
Poor service   Time, location, device, signal/performance test, outages and provider
diagnostics.
Unauthorised subscription   Opt-in record, confirmation message, renewal notices, deductions and
cancellation.
Arbitrary disconnection   Account status, notice, payment/dispute history, provisioning logs and reason
code.
Privacy/security incident   Access logs, disclosure path, event timeline, affected data and containment.
Preservation
Volatile network, charging and security logs may expire. Serious cases need early preservation
instructions and a documented chain of custody. Screenshots can support a claim, but source-system
records and reconciliation are usually needed for a defensible finding.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   186
A ticket number proves reporting, not the truth of every allegation. It is the start of an
evidence trail.

16.8 Billing, tariffs and data-usage disputes
A billing investigation reconstructs the service event and rating decision. It should not begin with the
assumption that either the consumer or billing platform is correct.
Layer   Question
Authorisation   Was the tariff/product approved or otherwise lawfully permitted?
Disclosure   Were price, unit, validity, renewal, restrictions and taxes explained?
Consent   Did the consumer actively choose the service or validly authorise renewal?
Measurement   What event or data volume was recorded, with what timestamp and unit?
Rating   Which tariff and bundle hierarchy converted usage into charge?
Balance update   Was credit deducted, reserved, reversed or delayed accurately?
Presentation   Could the consumer understand the bill, notifications and remaining balance?
Data depletion
Possible causes include video resolution, application updates, cloud backup, hotspot sharing,
malware, device synchronisation, metering error or incorrect bundle application. The provider should
explain recorded sessions sufficiently without disclosing protected network/security information;
consumer education should be evidence-based, not a dismissal.
Tariff transparency
Section 108 requires approval and publication for relevant individual-licensee tariffs, subject to the
statutory framework. The 2024 tariff-simplification direction seeks clearer and more comparable
offers. A headline price can mislead if validity, auto-renewal, out-of-bundle rate or eligibility is hidden.
Disputed amount
Good practice separates the disputed amount from undisputed liability, prevents disproportionate
collection while investigation is active where rules allow, and corrects consequential disconnection or
credit treatment if the bill was wrong.
Refund versus adjustment
A reversal removes an erroneous charge; a refund returns money; service credit supplies future
value; compensation recognises qualifying harm. The remedy must match the breach and should not
force a consumer to repurchase the benefit wrongly taken.
Bundle expiry and data exhaustion are different events. The first concerns time validity; the
second concerns consumption of the allowance.

16.9 Subscriptions, promotions and unsolicited services
A valid subscription should rest on informed, demonstrable consent. Silence, a hidden default or an
ambiguous click should not be converted into permission for recurring charges.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   187
Control point   Expected evidence
Offer   Provider, service, price, frequency, validity, renewal and cancellation.
Opt-in   Affirmative action attributable to the consumer.
Confirmation   Immediate message recording service and charge.
Renewal   Advance or timely notice and the agreed renewal basis.
Cancellation   Simple, effective channel and confirmation; no further charge after effective
cancellation.
Complaint/refund   Subscription log, content delivery, deductions and correction of unauthorised
charges.
Do Not Disturb
The Do-Not-Disturb framework gives consumers control over unsolicited marketing communications.
It should be distinguished from essential service messages, security notifications, emergency
information and communications the consumer specifically requested. The historical 2442 channel
and current implementation details should be verified before exact recall because harmonised-code
changes can affect presentation.
Promotional advertising
A promotion must disclose eligibility, duration, benefit, price, limitation, fair-use condition and what
happens when it ends. 'Free' is misleading when a mandatory charge or data consumption is
concealed. A claim such as 'unlimited' requires a clear explanation of any speed, volume or usage
restriction.
Value-added services
Responsibility can be shared among a network, aggregator and content provider, but the consumer
should not be pushed endlessly between them. Determine who obtained consent, delivered content,
applied the charge, controls cancellation and owes the refund.
Dark patterns
Interfaces that make acceptance prominent and cancellation obscure can undermine informed
choice. Examine the whole journey, not merely the existence of a terms link.
Consent is a lifecycle control: obtain it, record it, honour its scope and make withdrawal as
operationally effective as acceptance.

16.10 Advertising, packages and promotions
A truthful sentence can still mislead
An advertisement may contain technically true words while its overall impression is deceptive.
'Unlimited' can mislead if speed is substantially reduced after a hidden threshold. 'Free' can mislead if
activation requires an undisclosed paid bundle. NCC should examine the likely consumer impression,
material conditions and evidence supporting claims.
Risk   Example   Control
Headline-condition mismatch   Large bonus headline; tiny eligibility
restriction.
Prominent material conditions in the same
communication.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   188
Risk   Example   Control
Unsubstantiated superiority   'Fastest everywhere' without valid
comparative evidence.
Current, representative and reproducible
substantiation.
False scarcity   Countdown restarts repeatedly.   Genuine period and controlled campaign
configuration.
Automatic renewal   Trial becomes paid service without clear
consent.
Explicit disclosure, confirmation and
cancellation route.
Coverage exaggeration   Map or technology label presented as
guaranteed indoor service.
Explain methodology, limits and service
dependencies.
Price ambiguity   Tax, recurring charge or unit omitted.   Total payable price and charging basis.
Comparative advertising
A comparison should use like services, equivalent geography, time, devices and methods. An
operator should not select only its best cells or compare peak laboratory performance with a
competitor's measured median. NCC should be able to reproduce the claim from retained evidence.
Promotion lifecycle
Approve design and consumer terms before launch.
Test eligibility, charging, benefit delivery, renewal and opt-out in the live system.
Synchronise advert, agent script, application, USSD and billing configuration.
Monitor complaints, delivery failure and unexpected deductions during the campaign.
Stop or correct the offer where harm emerges.
Retain campaign version, approvals, audience, transactions and reconciliation.
Promotion regulation is both content control and systems assurance. A perfect advert cannot
rescue a billing engine that implements different rules.

16.11 Unsolicited communications and dnd
The consumer harm
Unwanted promotional calls and messages consume attention, create privacy concerns, enable
deception and can trigger charges. The 2024 General Code addresses unsolicited telemarketing,
while NCC's Do-Not-Disturb mechanism gives subscribers practical control over promotional
messaging.
Consent must be meaningful
Consent should identify the purpose and channel, be freely given where required, be recorded and be
withdrawable without unreasonable friction. A service contract should not be treated as blanket
permission for unrelated marketing. Silence, pre-ticked boxes or an obscure condition may not
establish genuine choice.
Concept   Meaning
Service message   Necessary communication about an existing service, security, bill or outage.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   189
Concept   Meaning
Marketing message   Communication intended to promote a product, service or commercial
response.
Transactional message   Message triggered by a requested transaction, such as confirmation.
Public-interest message   Communication authorised under an applicable emergency or public
framework.
Do-Not-Disturb preference   Recorded subscriber control over applicable promotional categories.
Why classification matters
A provider might label advertising as a 'service update' to bypass preferences. NCC should test
content, purpose, beneficiary and call to action rather than accept the label. Conversely, an essential
fraud alert should not be blocked merely because it arrives by the same channel as marketing.
Complaint evidence
Message content, sender identity and timestamp.
Subscriber preference and consent history at that time.
Campaign owner, service provider and originating connection.
Suppression-list processing and delivery logs.
Opt-out request, acknowledgement and subsequent messages.
Any charge or linked subscription activation.
Do-Not-Disturb is a consumer-control mechanism, not proof that every message is illegal.
Classify the communication and apply the relevant rule.

16.12 Quality failures, fault repair and compensation
Quality complaints may concern coverage, capacity, outage, dropped sessions, slow data, call setup,
messaging delay, fault repair or repeated local degradation. Use the end-to-end diagnostic method
explained in the service-quality chapter.
Individual and automatic redress
Individual complaints remain available, but the April 2026 NCC compensation framework adds
automatic airtime credit for qualifying mobile-network quality failure in confirmed Local Government
Areas. It aligns with the Consumer Code of Practice Regulations 2024 and Quality of Service
Regulations 2024 rather than replacing existing rights.
2026 framework element   Controlled position
Trigger   NCC confirms failure against applicable quality indicators for prolonged or
repeated poor experience.
Location   Affected Local Government Areas are identified and published.
Eligibility   Affected Nigerian-operator line with at least one billed outgoing activity in the
relevant period, subject to framework rules.
Coverage   Voice, text messaging and data service failures; individuals and corporate
customers can qualify.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   190
2026 framework element   Controlled position
Form   Automatic unrestricted airtime credit; individual application is not required.
Calculation inputs   Billed usage, operator performance in the area and qualifying activity.
Notification   Operator informs the subscriber when the credit is applied.
Enforcement   Compensation can coexist with regulatory penalty in severe or repeated
cases.
Exceptions and causation
Fibre cuts, theft, vandalism, natural disaster and other exceptional events require NCC review; they
are not an automatic blanket defence. Examine foreseeability, prevention, redundancy, response and
the framework's force-majeure treatment.
Compensation is not cure
Airtime credit addresses consumer value but does not restore infrastructure. NCC should verify
network remediation, root cause and recurrence. A provider must not treat compensation as
permission to continue poor performance.
The 2026 mechanism is automatic for qualifying confirmed cases; it is not a payment to
every subscriber who reports one short interruption.

16.13 Privacy, security and digital-safety complaints
Communications providers hold registration, contact, traffic, billing, location and support records.
Consumer protection and data protection overlap, but NCC, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission,
law-enforcement bodies and courts have different mandates.
Complaint   Immediate priority
SIM swap/account takeover   Secure service, preserve transaction/agent logs, restore lawful control and
coordinate affected institutions.
Data disclosure   Contain access, identify data/recipients, preserve evidence and assess
notification duties.
Harassment/spam   Preserve message/origin evidence, block/report where appropriate and
distinguish marketing from criminal threat.
Caller-ID spoofing   Trace signalling and ingress; do not accuse the displayed-number holder
without evidence.
Child online harm   Use safety reporting, parental/usage controls and competent
law-enforcement/content routes.
Stolen device   Block relevant equipment/service identifiers where lawful, protect account and
warn against remote-access fraud.
Data minimisation in complaint handling
A complaint team should request only data necessary for the case, use secure transfer, restrict
access and redact published examples. Consumers should not be asked to share passwords, full
personal identification numbers or one-time passwords.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   191
Breach communication
Notice should explain what happened, affected information, likely risk, protective steps, provider
action and contact channel. Premature certainty and vague reassurance both undermine trust; label
what is known and what remains under investigation.
Cross-regulator referral
NCC should retain the telecommunications aspect while referring or coordinating the privacy,
competition, financial or criminal aspect with the competent body. Referral is not abandonment:
ownership, consent, response expectations and feedback should be recorded.
Privacy harm does not cease to be a consumer issue merely because another regulator
also has jurisdiction.

16.14 Protection of consumer information
Why communications data is sensitive
Subscriber identity, contact details, National Identification Number linkage, biometrics, location,
usage, complaints, billing and communications metadata can reveal intimate patterns. A licensee
needs lawful purpose, appropriate security and controlled retention; customer-care convenience is
not permission for unrestricted access.
Principle   Operational meaning
Purpose limitation   Use information for the authorised, stated function.
Data minimisation   Collect and expose only what the task requires.
Accuracy   Correct wrong current records while preserving lawful history.
Access control   Grant privileges by role, need and risk.
Security   Protect data at collection, transit, storage, use and disposal.
Retention   Keep information for the applicable period and dispose securely thereafter.
Accountability   Record access, change, disclosure, export and incident response.
Customer-care access
An agent may need to verify an account and view the minimum fields necessary to solve a case. Full
call-detail records, biometrics or identity documents should require stronger role, purpose and audit.
Screen masking, controlled search, download restriction and alerting reduce casual misuse.
Information sharing
Requests from NCC, another regulator or law-enforcement body require legal authority, scope,
identity verification and secure transmission. A staff member should not disclose information because
a request appears urgent or carries an official-looking letter. The case record should preserve
request, approval, data extracted and recipient.
Breach and complaint
Contain exposure, preserve evidence, assess affected data and persons, notify through lawful
channels, correct the weakness and provide redress where required. Do not use the compromised
contact channel as the only authentication method for the affected consumer.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   192
Privacy and consumer protection reinforce trust; they do not prevent every lawful regulatory use.
The question is authority, necessity, proportionality, security and accountability.

16.15 Accessibility, inclusion and required services
Section 107 allows NCC to determine required applications services, including emergency, directory
assistance, operator assistance and services for disabled consumers. For emergency services, the
Act emphasises a universal number and seamless, ubiquitous, reliable end-to-end infrastructure.
Barrier   Inclusive response
Hearing impairment   Text, relay or other accessible channel where provided; do not require
voice-only complaint handling.
Visual impairment   Screen-reader-compatible portal, structured text and accessible documents.
Mobility/geographic barrier   Remote channels and authorised representation instead of mandatory
physical visit.
Low literacy/language   Plain language, guided form and verbal explanation without removing
informed consent.
Digital exclusion   Telephone and physical alternatives to online-only processes.
Financial vulnerability   Free complaint channels and proportionate verification/collection practices.
Emergency access
Reliability depends on number configuration, originating network, interconnection, emergency centre
capacity, location information where supported, power and trained response. A universal number that
rings nowhere useful is not an end-to-end service.
Universal design
Designing accessible support from the start is more reliable and often cheaper than case-by-case
exception. Test with affected users and measure abandonment, resolution and satisfaction by
channel.
Authorised representatives
A representative may help a child, person with disability, corporate customer or deceased
subscriber's estate. Verify authority proportionately and disclose only what the representation
permits.
Consumer education
Outreach should be usable, current and measurable. It should explain rights, responsibilities,
complaint channels, scam risks and service choices, then test whether target groups understood and
changed behaviour.
Equality is not forcing every consumer through one identical channel; it is providing fair access to
the same protective outcome.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   193

16.16 Remedies: correction, refund, compensation and enforcement
Remedy   Purpose
Explanation/apology   Acknowledge error and clarify action; insufficient alone where loss remains.
Correction   Fix account, registration, tariff, route, subscription or complaint record.
Restoration   Return service or access to the lawful state.
Refund/reversal   Return or remove an unsupported charge.
Service credit/compensation   Provide prescribed or proportionate value for qualifying failure or harm.
Specific performance   Require the provider to complete an obligation, where lawful and feasible.
Direction/enforcement   Correct and deter public regulatory breach beyond the individual case.
Systemic remediation   Identify all similarly affected consumers and correct them without requiring
separate complaints.
Remedy design
Connect remedy to established breach and actual affected person.
Stop continuing harm before debating final quantum.
Restore the consumer as nearly as practicable to the correct position.
Include consequential service effects caused by the provider's error.
Use automatic/bulk correction where records identify the affected class.
Specify deadline, evidence and owner.
Verify implementation independently or through reliable system evidence.
Preserve appeal/review rights and explain unresolved issues.
Penalty is different
A regulatory penalty punishes or deters breach and is not automatically paid to the consumer. Refund
and compensation repair consumer harm. Both can coexist, as the 2026 quality-compensation
framework expressly recognises for serious or repeated violations.
No double counting
Where several mechanisms cover the same loss, record what each remedy addresses. Avoid both
under-compensation and unexplained duplication; statutory entitlements must still be honoured.
A refund returns an improper charge; compensation addresses qualifying harm; a fine is a
public enforcement consequence.

16.17 Complaint system design and data governance
A complaint-management platform should create one reconstructable case across telephone, portal,
email, social media, letter and provider integration. Multiple channels should not create duplicate
unlinked cases.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   194
Case object   Essential controls
Identity/authority   Proportionate verification, representative authority and protected personal
data.
Ticket   Unique identifier, source, received time, priority, owner and service-level
clock.
Issue   Controlled category plus consumer's own narrative and requested outcome.
Evidence   Source, timestamp, integrity, confidentiality and retention.
Provider action   Request, response, commitments, attachments and escalation.
Decision   Facts, instrument, analysis, remedy, reason and approver.
Communication   Accessible notices, delivery proof, consumer response and satisfaction.
Closure   Verified remedy, financial reconciliation, root cause and systemic link.
Service-level clocks
The system must calculate the correct deadline for the complaint category and instrument, record
lawful pauses and warn before breach. A generic deadline can be wrong for fraud, emergency, billing,
fault repair or information request.
Taxonomy
Categories should be mutually intelligible and stable enough for trend analysis: billing, quality,
provisioning, value-added services, number/identity, privacy/security, customer care and
accessibility. Preserve the original allegation when reclassifying.
Automation
Automated triage can detect duplicates, urgency and patterns, but human review remains necessary
for adverse findings, sensitive identity decisions and remedy. Record model/version, confidence,
override and source data where automation materially influences action.
False closure controls
Do not close on provider promise alone.
Reconcile refund or credit to the account.
Confirm restored service through test or consumer contact where feasible.
Reopen automatically when the same remedy fails within a defined period.
Separate unreachable consumer from resolved complaint.
Sample closed cases for quality assurance.
A complaint database is regulatory intelligence. Its value comes from accurate facts, verified
remedies and patterns, not the volume of tickets marked closed.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   195
Signal   Regulatory question
Same charge across many lines   Was a tariff, bundle or billing configuration wrong sector-wide or
provider-wide?
Spike after system release   Did change control, testing or rollback fail?
Geographic quality cluster   Is there an outage, capacity deficit, fibre cut or power/site problem?
Repeated unresolved tickets   Is first-level complaint handling structurally inadequate?
Identical rejection language   Is automation or policy denying valid cases without investigation?
Disproportionate vulnerable-group
harm
Is the channel or product inaccessible or discriminatory in effect?
Root-cause ladder
Ask why the event occurred, why the control failed to prevent it, why monitoring failed to detect it and
why governance allowed recurrence. Correct the deepest supported cause, not only the visible
transaction.
Bulk redress
Where provider records can identify all affected consumers, requiring each to complain individually is
inefficient and unfair. Define the affected population, calculation, notification, exception route and
audit sample.
Publication
Publishing aggregate trends and regulatory outcomes can deter breach and educate users, but
protect personal and commercially confidential information. Explain definitions so complaint counts
are not misread as failure without considering subscriber scale and channel changes.
Consumer satisfaction
Resolution rate alone is inadequate. Measure timeliness, first-contact resolution, recurrence, remedy
accuracy, accessibility, abandonment and satisfaction. A consumer may be dissatisfied with a correct
lawful decision, so satisfaction complements rather than replaces compliance evidence.
A rising complaint count may mean worsening service, improved awareness, better
access, reclassification or all four. Investigate the denominator and context.

16.19 Jurisdiction, coordination and fairness
Issue   Possible competent bodies
Telecom service and licence
obligation
NCC and provider under NCA/subsidiary instruments.
Personal-data processing   Nigeria Data Protection Commission, NCC within sector rules, and courts as
applicable.
General consumer/competition issue   Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, NCC sector
powers and coordination mechanisms.
Banking or payment loss   Financial institution and Central Bank framework, with NCC on telecom
identity/network evidence.
Fraud, threat or theft   Law-enforcement agencies, with regulated entities preserving and lawfully
supplying evidence.
Advertising/content   NCC plus another competent advertising, broadcasting or content authority
depending on the service.
No forum ping-pong
A multi-issue complaint needs a lead, referral record, consumer explanation and feedback
arrangement. Each body should handle its lawful part. The consumer should not be required to
understand government architecture before urgent harm is contained.
Fairness to providers
Consumer protection is not automatic acceptance of allegations. Give the provider the case,
reasonable opportunity and relevant evidence to respond; test contrary material; manage
confidentiality; and explain findings. Urgent interim protection may precede a final liability decision.
Contract and regulation
Contract terms define the service relationship but cannot lawfully remove statutory or regulatory
rights. Equally, NCC should not rewrite every commercial disappointment into a breach where clear
lawful terms were honoured.
Courts and alternative dispute resolution
Section 105 supports NCC complaint and alternative-resolution processes. Court rights and other
remedies depend on applicable law and exhaustion requirements. Do not present NCC mediation as
a final constitutional bar to judicial recourse.
Good coordination preserves jurisdiction while producing one coherent consumer journey and a
defensible evidence record.

16.20 Applied level 10 scenarios
Scenario 1 - Data disappears overnight
Secure the account; obtain bundle/usage timelines; check application updates, hotspot, session and
rating records; explain findings in plain language; refund if metering/rating was wrong; educate only
after evidence; test for a wider billing defect.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   197
Scenario 2 - Provider closes without refund
Reopen or challenge closure because an apology is not the ordered remedy. Reconcile the financial
transaction, verify the account, compensate consequential disconnection where applicable and
examine false-closure controls.
Scenario 3 - Consumer bypasses provider
Explain the section 105 operator-first route and help obtain a ticket. If the provider channel is
unavailable or the matter involves urgent continuing identity/safety harm, record the facts and take
the lawful protective/escalation path rather than mechanically rejecting it.
Scenario 4 - Unauthorised recurring service
Demand opt-in, confirmation, delivery, renewal and cancellation logs; stop future deductions; refund
unsupported charges; inspect aggregator/network roles; search for similarly affected lines and
enforce where systematic.
Scenario 5 - Whole area has poor service
Combine complaints with location, network indicators and independent evidence. Assess the 2026
compensation trigger, publish/verify eligible area where directed, ensure automatic airtime credits
and require network remediation separately.
Scenario 6 - Complaint includes banking loss after SIM swap
Restore lawful telecom control and preserve swap/agent logs urgently; coordinate the financial and
criminal aspects with competent institutions; distinguish telecom process failure from bank
authentication failure; avoid promising recovery NCC cannot lawfully order.
Scenario 7 - Blind consumer cannot use portal
Offer an accessible channel immediately, record the barrier, test portal compatibility and require
systemic accessibility correction. Equal rights do not require an identical unusable interface.
Scenario 8 - Provider blames vandalism
Verify cause, duration, affected users, redundancy, response and prior incidents. Apply the
compensation framework's exceptional-event review and quality obligations; do not accept or reject
the label without evidence.
MODEL ANSWER FORMULA
Right/obligation   →   first-level ticket and urgency   →   evidence and applicable instrument   →   fair provider
response   →   finding   →   remedy and systemic check   →   communication   →   verified closure and
regulatory learning.
Provision/instrument   Recall
NCA section 104   Minimum quality, reasonable treatment and adequate complaint handling.
NCA section 105   NCC complaint powers; procedures/alternative resolution; provider process
first.

and systemic check   →   communication   →   verified closure and
regulatory learning.
Provision/instrument   Recall
NCA section 104   Minimum quality, reasonable treatment and adequate complaint handling.
NCA section 105   NCC complaint powers; procedures/alternative resolution; provider process
first.
NCA section 106   Approved consumer code: requirements, disputes, compensation,
information, billing and annual review.
NCA section 107   Required applications including emergency and services for disabled
consumers.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   198
Provision/instrument   Recall
Consumer Code 2024   Current published general consumer-protection framework on NCC's register.
Quality Regulations 2024 / Business
Rules 2026
Current quality framework and implementation layer; preserve chronology.
April 2026 compensation mechanism   Automatic airtime credit for qualifying confirmed mobile quality failures in
identified areas.
CAB second-level support   Provider first; unresolved consumer escalates with ticket through 622, portal
and other official channels.
High-value distinctions
Do not confuse   Correct distinction
Complaint/redress   Allegation and process / actual correction of established harm.
Closure/resolution   Administrative state / verified remedy.
Refund/compensation/fine   Return charge / repair qualifying harm / public sanction.
Education/excuse   Help informed use / improper shifting of provider liability.
Individual/systemic case   One consumer outcome / root cause and all affected consumers.
Mediation/enforcement   Facilitated settlement / exercise of regulatory power.
NCC Promotion Study Guide   199

Chapter 17
Universal access and the Universal Service
Provision Fund
A competitive market can expand rapidly while leaving some communities without affordable, usable
service. Universal-service policy begins by identifying that gap and selecting a sustainable
intervention, then places funding and delivery within a defined statutory structure.

17.1 Why the market may leave gaps
Commercial deployment follows expected return
A licensee invests where expected revenue can cover capital, operating cost, financing and risk.
Sparse populations, difficult terrain, insecurity, low incomes, weak power, expensive transport and
uncertain demand can make some communities commercially unattractive even though connectivity
would create large social benefits.
Barrier   How it creates a gap
High fixed cost   Tower, fibre, power and core integration cost is spread across few users.
Low ability to pay   Social need exists but forecast revenue is insufficient.
Demand uncertainty   Operator cannot confidently predict take-up after construction.
Complementary infrastructure   No grid, road, device, skills or local content reduces usefulness.
Geography and security   Terrain, flood, distance, vandalism or conflict raise build and maintenance
cost.
Coordination failure   Several actors wait for another to supply backhaul, power or anchor demand.
Social value can exceed private return
Connectivity can improve education, health, agriculture, safety, public administration and market
access. Those benefits may accrue to society rather than the network operator's bill. A targeted
public intervention can therefore be justified where evidence shows a genuine access gap and
additional social benefit.
Intervention still has a cost
Universal service money comes from sector and public resources. Funding an inefficient or
unnecessary project can distort competition, crowd out commercial investment and waste
contributions. The case must establish need, additionality, proportionality and sustainability.
A rural location is not automatically unserved, and an urban location is not automatically
well served. Use current geographic and service evidence.

17.2 Access, service and meaningful use
Universal access
Universal access generally focuses on reasonable availability of communications to a community or
defined population, sometimes through a shared facility such as a community centre, school or public
access point. It asks whether people can reach a communications opportunity even if every
household has no individual connection.
Universal service
Universal service moves toward availability of defined services to individual users or households on
reasonable terms. The exact scope is set by national policy and the regulatory framework; it can
evolve as essential communications expectations change.
Layer   Question
Physical access   Is infrastructure or signal present and reachable?
Availability   Can an eligible user obtain a working service?
Affordability   Can the target population reasonably pay for device, activation and recurring
use?
Accessibility   Can persons with disabilities, language or literacy barriers use it?
Adoption   Do intended beneficiaries subscribe or attend?
Meaningful use   Does service have adequate quality, safety, skills and relevant applications?
Outcome   Does connectivity improve the intended social or economic condition?
Coverage is not inclusion
A map may show fourth-generation coverage while residents lack devices, electricity, affordable data
or digital skills. Conversely, a shared institutional connection may create valuable education or health
outcomes without household subscription. Evaluation must match the intervention's purpose.
The moving baseline
A voice-access objective from an earlier era may not satisfy a present need for usable broadband.
Expansion should be financially realistic, technology-neutral where appropriate and guided by current
policy rather than assuming every community needs identical infrastructure.
Digital inclusion is a chain: infrastructure, service, affordability, device, skills, trust, relevant content
and sustained use.

17.3 Section 112 - designing universal service provision
The Commission must consider, design and determine a system promoting widespread availability
and usage of network services and application services throughout Nigeria. The mechanism
encourages network facilities and services for institutions, unserved or underserved areas and
underserved groups.
Four examinable ideas
The duty belongs to NCC: consider, design and determine a system.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   201
The objective includes both availability and usage; infrastructure alone is not the complete statutory
idea.
The scope covers network facilities, network services and application services.
Beneficiaries include institutions, geographic areas and groups within the community.
The universal-service organ is not a communications service provider
Section 112(2) prevents an organ created under this Part from constituting itself as a communications
service provider. The architecture is designed to facilitate, fund and supervise provision through
eligible actors, not to turn the Fund or Board into another operator.

17.4 Section 113 - determining the gap
NCC's determination must define institutions, unserved areas, underserved areas and underserved
groups. For areas, the Act permits attention to service availability, competition and the commercial
viability of installing facilities or providing services. For groups, it permits attention to service
availability and barriers to use. For institutions, NCC should consider educational, health and other
social-infrastructural needs.
Category   Statutory lens
Unserved/underserved area   Availability, level of competition and commercial viability.
Underserved group   Availability to the group and barriers to using available service.
Institution   Educational, health and other socio-infrastructural needs of Nigerians.
Section 113 does not define an underserved area only by rural location. Availability,
competition and commercial viability are statutory considerations.

17.5 Section 114 - the fund, its sources and safeguards
Establishment
Section 114 establishes the Universal Service Provision Fund and requires it to be controlled and
operated in the manner specified in Chapter VII of the Act.
Sources
Source   Meaning
National Assembly appropriation   Money specifically appropriated to the Fund from time to time.
Commission contribution   A portion of annual levies paid to NCC by licensees.
Other lawful assets   Gifts, loans, aids and other assets that specifically accrue to the Fund.
Expenses
Administrative and operational expenses are funded from the Fund. The Act expressly includes
remuneration and allowances for Board members, full-time NCC staff assigned to the Secretariat or
other Secretariat staff, the Fund Manager, and operational expenses of the Board, Secretariat and
Fund Managers.

NCC Promotion Study Guide   202
Separation and audit
NCC must ensure that the Fund remains totally separate from the Commission's Fund under Part IV
of Chapter II and is transparently maintained and operated. Independent auditors appointed by the
Board must audit it annually. The report is presented to the National Assembly and published, and the
auditors must be drawn from the list approved by the Federal Accountant-General.
Control   Why it matters
Separate Fund   Prevents universal-service resources from becoming indistinguishable from
ordinary NCC funds.
Transparent maintenance   Allows contributions, investments, disbursements and expenses to be traced.
Independent annual audit   Provides external financial assurance.
Legislative presentation and
publication
Creates public and institutional accountability.
Licensees do not pay contributions directly into an undefined project pool merely because
the Fund exists. Follow the statutory source, assessment, collection and accounting
framework.
